children: Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd. (RVNL) has emerged as the lowest bidder (L1) for a ₹348.49-crore project awarded by East Coast Railway to upgrade the Vadlapudi Wagon Workshop in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

The project involves increasing the workshop's periodic overhaul (POH) capacity from 300 to 600 wagons at Vadlapudi in the Waltair division of East Coast Railway. RVNL will have 24 months to complete the work.

This is the latest railway project secured by RVNL from East Coast Railway. On September 19, the company announced that it had received a letter of acceptance (LoA) worth ₹404.88 crore for work related to the development of a third railway line along the Nergundi–Barang and Khurda Road–Vizianagaram sections.

The contract, valued at ₹404.88 crore, including goods and services tax (GST), covers a 385-km stretch of the Bhadrak–Vizianagaram section. This includes 22 km between Nergundi and Barang and 363 km between Khurda Road and Vizianagaram.
RVNL shares ended 2.05% lower at ₹191 on Friday. The stock has declined nearly 50% so far this year.

title: RVNL emerges as L1 bidder for ₹348 crore East Coast Railway project
